speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is concerning, as the presence of fever, rigidity, and confusion is not typical for a migraine; these symptoms strongly suggest a central nervous system infection like meningitis or encephalitis. I need to review your test results immediately to see if they confirm an infectious process or reveal metabolic causes.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Meningoencephalitis (Pending CSF and CBC results)
